    body {

      line-height: 1.5;
    }
    html { -webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; text-size-adjust: 100%; }
    h1, h2, h3 { line-height: 1.2; text-wrap: balance; }
    p { text-wrap: pretty; }
    p, li, h1, h2, h3 { overflow-wrap: break-word; }
    img, svg, video { max-width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; }
    :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid currentColor; outline-offset: 2px; }
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
      *, *::before, *::after { animation: none !important; transition: none !important; scroll-behavior: auto !important; }
    }

`0.html` is already a solid, empty starter template. It has the viewport and color-scheme meta tags, a readable line length, balanced heading wrapping, focus outlines and reduced-motion handling. The page has no content yet, so there isn't much to improve without knowing what it's for.

The only real gaps I see:

- **The `description` meta tag is empty**, and the title is just "0". Both need real text, which depends on what the page is about.
- **Form controls don't use the page font.** Buttons and inputs fall back to the browser's default font. One line fixes it: `button, input, select, textarea { font: inherit; }`.
- **There's no skip link and no `<header>`/`<footer>`.** These only matter once the page has navigation.

I haven't changed anything yet. What should the page be (a landing page, an article, a tool)? I can fill in the content, title and description to match. Or I can just apply the small fixes above to the template as it is.
